title: Chapter 66 — The Designer Referral Engine
intro: Turning designer relationships into systematic referral flows between designers, builders, and homeowners.

sections.title: Why Designers Refer
sections.content:
A designer who trusts your product knowledge and delivery reliability will refer you to three audiences: their builder partners, their clients (homeowners), and other designers. Each referral type has different value and requires different cultivation.

Designer-to-builder referrals are the most valuable because they create new trade accounts. 'My appliance rep is excellent — you should use them on your next project.' That single sentence from a respected designer is worth more than 50 cold calls.

Designer-to-client referrals drive retail premium sales. 'Go see [your name] at [store] — tell them I sent you. They will take care of you.' These clients arrive pre-sold, pre-qualified, and ready to buy premium.

sections.title: Building the Engine
sections.content:
After every successful project with a designer, ask explicitly: 'Do you have any builder partners who might benefit from working with us? I would love an introduction.'

Create a reciprocal referral system. When a retail customer mentions they are renovating, ask: 'Are you working with a designer? I know several excellent ones — would you like a recommendation?' When you refer clients to a designer, the designer reciprocates. The engine feeds itself.

Track referral source in your CRM. Know which designers produce the most referrals and invest proportionally in those relationships. A designer who refers 5 clients per year deserves the best service, the fastest quotes, and the first invitation to every event.

sections.title: Keeping the Engine Running
sections.content: Referral engines stall when you stop feeding them. Keep designers informed about new products, new rebates, and new capabilities. Send a quarterly update: 'Here is what is new that your clients will love.' Stay visible. Stay valuable. Stay referable.
